summary.headline: The Golf Committee funded an Audubon consultant shortfall and finalized advocacy plans for a major golf course irrigation article at Special Town Meeting.
summary.summary: The Southborough Golf Committee voted to allocate up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to cover a budget gap for an Audubon International certification consultant and approved paying $500 in overdue dues. Members spent most of the meeting preparing for the upcoming Special Town Meeting, where voters will consider additional funding for a course irrigation project and an extension of $550,000 in previously approved CPA funds set to expire in December. The committee opted against asking to amend or split the warrant article on the floor and made plans to use print handouts after learning that non-sponsors cannot project slides on the main auditorium screen.

topics.title: Audubon certification dues and consultant funding
topics.summary: The committee reviewed proposals to assist the golf course with achieving Audubon International certification. Conservation Works submitted the sole proposal at $18,400, which exceeds the available Community Preservation Act project balance by approximately $4,500. Members voted to pay past-due membership fees and committed up to $4,500 from the golf revolving fund to bridge the gap so procurement can finalize the contract.
key_details: Audubon International dues of $500 were past due, with another $500 annual renewal due in November.
Conservation Works submitted the lone bid of $18,400, about $4,500 over the remaining CPA grant balance.
The committee plans to work with the vendor to trim costs, including potentially dropping a $650 golfer focus group task.
Members voted unanimously to authorize up to $4,500 from the revolving fund to cover the deficit.
Town procurement staff will be engaged to formalize the consultant agreement.
topics.outcome: Approved paying $500 in dues and up to $4,500 from the revolving fund for the consultant.

topics.title: Special Town Meeting irrigation article preparation
topics.summary: The committee strategized on how to present and advocate for the Community Preservation Act warrant article at the upcoming Special Town Meeting. The article seeks roughly $350,000 in new CPA funds and $100,000 from the revolving fund for an irrigation system overhaul, while also extending the sunset date for $550,000 in previously authorized funds that expire December 30. Members discussed whether to ask the Community Preservation Committee to split or amend the article if passage looks doubtful, but agreed to push forward with the full article as written.
key_details: The article adds roughly $350,000 in CPA money and $100,000 in revolving funds to existing $550,000 authorizations expiring December 30.
The committee chose not to pursue a floor amendment to decouple the sunset clause extension from the new funding request.
Town officials notified the committee that only designated article sponsors may display slides on the main screen, preventing committee members from projecting visual aids during debate.
The committee will distribute paper flyers and mount informational posters on registration tables instead.
Members plan to recruit local golfers and senior residents to speak at the microphone during debate.
topics.outcome: Decided not to seek article amendments and agreed on a print-based outreach strategy for Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: If the warrant article fails, the town risks losing $550,000 in previously approved CPA funds and jeopardizing needed irrigation upgrades to preserve the town-owned golf course.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved the minutes of the prior meeting with a minor clerical correction and confirmed logistical plans for its next formal sessions.
key_details: Approved prior meeting minutes with an editorial spelling correction to the chair's name.
Noted written confirmation from town administration that voter handouts may be placed on tables at registration.
Agreed to hold a brief posted meeting before Town Meeting on Saturday morning, followed by the next regular meeting in November.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved and future meeting dates established.

votes.motion: Approve $500 from the revolving fund to pay past-due Audubon International annual membership dues.
Authorize up to $4,500 from the revolving fund to cover the budget shortfall for the Audubon consultant contract.

upcoming.what: Special Town Meeting vote on golf course irrigation warrant article
